title: Eliciting Frequency-Conditioned Spatial Dynamics for Long-Term Spatio-Temporal Forecasting

problem.claim: Long-term spatio-temporal forecasting must capture spatial dynamics within entangled long-term temporal patterns.

gap.claim: Existing approaches lack a unified temporal decomposition scheme that generalizes across urban scenarios and struggle to learn spatial correlations evolving across co-existing temporal patterns over long horizons.

contributions.claim: FCoSD is an end-to-end framework for eliciting frequency-conditioned spatial dynamics in long-term spatio-temporal forecasting.
A learnable Gaussian soft frequency-band mask adaptively decomposes long-term temporal patterns into low-, mid-, and high-frequency components.
A frequency-conditioned spatial Mamba module captures dynamic spatial dependencies within each frequency band, and a multi-band gated fusion module integrates the representations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on multiple real-world spatio-temporal datasets.
The authors report that FCoSD outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Long-term spatio-temporal forecasting is presented as important for public service management and urban renewal.
Existing methods are described as limited by inadequate temporal decomposition and evolving spatial-correlation modeling over long horizons.
FCoSD reorganizes raw signals into frequency-aware components and learns spatial dynamics tailored to each component.
The framework uses adaptive frequency-band masking, frequency-conditioned spatial Mamba, and multi-band gated fusion.
Experiments on multiple real-world datasets are reported to show superior performance over state-of-the-art methods.

source_observation.claim: The framework decomposes long-term temporal patterns into frequency bands and models spatial dependencies separately within each band.

interpretation.claim: Separating temporal frequencies may help isolate spatial dynamics that evolve at different temporal scales.

application.claim: For long-horizon spatio-temporal forecasting, consider adaptive frequency decomposition paired with frequency-specific spatial modeling.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported urban scenarios or datasets.

unknowns: Dataset identities, sizes, splits, and evaluation metrics are not specified.
Baseline identities and quantitative performance differences are not specified.
The abstract does not report ablations, computational costs, or failure cases.
